question_text: Find, correct to 3 significant figures, all unknown sides:

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct calculation for mean and locating middle terms for median
Accurate mean and median values with units

subparts.solution: $\text{mean} = \frac{7.5 + 6.8 + \dots + 8.5}{30} = \frac{233.1}{30} = 7.77\text{ hours}$. As $n = 30$, $\frac{n+1}{2} = 15.5$, so the median is the average of the 15th and 16th values. The 15th value is 7.5 and 16th value is 7.6. $\therefore \text{median} = \frac{7.5 + 7.6}{2} = 7.55\text{ hours}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The mean sums all observations and divides by $n=30$. The median is the average of the 15th and 16th ordered data points.
step_by_step: Sum the 30 values to get $233.1$; divide by $30$ to get $7.77$.
Arrange the data in ascending order.
Identify the 15th value ($7.5$) and the 16th value ($7.6$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Miscounting sorted positions and selecting incorrect values for the median.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An outlier is an extreme data point that lies significantly outside the general pattern of the data.
step_by_step: Inspect the dataset: most values range between 5.8 and 9.1.
The maximum value 11.5 is far greater than 9.1.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Identifying a value at the lower end when the extreme value is at the upper end.

mark_breakdown.desc: Recalculating mean and median with n = 29
Correct recalculated mean and median values

subparts.solution: $\text{mean} = \frac{7.5 + 6.8 + \dots + 8.5}{29} = \frac{221.6}{29} \approx 7.64\text{ hours}$. As $n = 29$ with the outlier removed, $\frac{n+1}{2} = 15$. The 15th value in the ordered data set is 7.5. $\therefore \text{median} = 7.5\text{ hours}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Removing an outlier decreases sample size to $n=29$. The new mean uses the reduced sum divided by 29, and the new median is the 15th ordered value.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing by 30 instead of 29 after removing the outlier.
